subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: Should a Slack DM/main session be allowed to recall the agent’s own outbound channel message content, and what account, sender-authorization, retention, and deletion boundary must govern that access?
rationale: Current isolation is intentional and the narrow request cannot be implemented safely until maintainers define who may trigger recall and which channel content may cross into a DM context.

options.title: Scoped self-activity ledger
options.body: Store and expose only agent-authored outbound Slack content with strict team/account, destination, retention, deletion, and requester-authorization checks.

options.title: Use agent-wide session visibility
options.body: Document an opt-in tools.sessions.visibility=agent path, accepting that it exposes broader inbound and outbound transcript content than this request needs.

options.title: Preserve isolation
options.body: Keep channel content unavailable from DM sessions and document explicit memory or session-tool workflows for operators who accept broader access.

recommendation.title: Scoped self-activity ledger
recommendation.body: Store and expose only agent-authored outbound Slack content with strict team/account, destination, retention, deletion, and requester-authorization checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion and recent routing/outbound history make steipete the strongest available owner for the cross-session privacy contract.
